domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In the past, mechanically ventilated patients with delirium were treated how, and what was the paradigm shift?
answer: Previously treated with mechanical restraint plus sedatives or paralytics; now evidence shows this worsened outcomes; current approach minimizes sedation and promotes early mobilization
rationale: Physical restraint and heavy sedation worsen delirium through immobility and drug accumulation; ABCDEF bundle (awakening, breathing, coordination, delirium, early mobility, family) improves outcomes.
confusable_with: Deep sedation being protective against delirium

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What is the distinction between emergence delirium and postoperative delirium?
answer: Emergence delirium occurs acutely during recovery from anesthesia; postoperative delirium develops over hours to days postoperatively and is separate
rationale: Emergence delirium is typically self-limited and resolves as anesthetics clear; postoperative delirium has distinct multifactorial causes and prolonged course.
confusable_with: Treating emergence delirium identically to postoperative delirium

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What ICU complication can develop in more than 50% of brain-dead patients that leads to diabetes insipidus and adrenal insufficiency?
answer: Pituitary failure occurs in more than 50% of brain-dead patients, causing diabetes insipidus and secondary adrenal insufficiency
rationale: Pituitary ischemia/herniation in brain death abolishes ADH and ACTH secretion, producing DI and adrenal insufficiency complicating donor management.
confusable_with: SIADH developing in brain death (opposite, DI is the typical finding)

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What structures have been proposed to facilitate patient and family-centered care decisions in the ICU?
answer: Family meetings, shared decision-making frameworks, and ICU care conferences facilitate patient and family-centered care
rationale: ICU patients often lack decision-making capacity; structured family communication reduces conflict, improves end-of-life decision quality, and decreases family distress.
confusable_with: Physician unilateral decision-making as standard ICU practice

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In older adult patients, what postoperative cognitive complication requires distinguishing from intraoperative awareness or substance withdrawal?
answer: Postoperative delirium or cognitive dysfunction (POCD) in older adults must be distinguished from awareness, withdrawal, and other neurological events
rationale: POCD and delirium are common in elderly after major surgery and anesthesia; misdiagnosis delays appropriate management and may worsen outcomes.
confusable_with: All post-op confusion in elderly being sedation residual

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: Malnutrition in the perioperative period is associated with what complications?
answer: Malnutrition increases infection rates, wound healing complications, and overall perioperative morbidity
rationale: Protein and micronutrient deficits impair immune function, collagen synthesis, and muscle strength, all critical for surgical recovery.
confusable_with: Malnutrition only affecting long-term outcomes, not perioperative complications

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In critical illness, what nitrogen balance consideration drives ICU protein provision goals?
answer: Critical illness causes catabolism with increased protein breakdown; ICU nutrition aims to provide adequate protein (1.2-2 g/kg/day) to limit muscle wasting
rationale: Hypercatabolism in sepsis and trauma increases protein requirements; underfeeding protein causes muscle wasting, prolonged ventilation, and impaired immunity.
confusable_with: Standard 0.8 g/kg/day protein adequate in critically ill patients

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What is the preferred route for ICU nutrition if the gastrointestinal tract is functional?
answer: Enteral nutrition is preferred over parenteral nutrition when the GI tract is functional; early enteral feeding reduces infectious complications
rationale: Enteral nutrition maintains intestinal mucosal integrity, reduces bacterial translocation, and avoids catheter-related bloodstream infections of TPN.
confusable_with: TPN being equivalent or superior to enteral nutrition in all ICU patients

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In postcardiac surgery ICU management, patients are generally extubated early to reduce what specific morbidity?
answer: Early extubation after cardiac surgery decreases postoperative morbidity by reducing ventilator-associated pneumonia and ICU complications
rationale: Prolonged intubation in cardiac surgical patients increases pulmonary infection risk and delays mobilization; fast-track cardiac protocols improve outcomes.
confusable_with: Routine overnight intubation for all cardiac surgical patients

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What is the range of conditions that ICU specialists must address that extends beyond the classic surgical domain?
answer: ICU practice addresses nosocomial infections, hemodynamic instability, respiratory failure, metabolic disorders, nutrition, and end-of-life care
rationale: Critical care medicine requires cross-disciplinary expertise integrating surgery, internal medicine, pharmacology, and ethics.
confusable_with: ICU care being limited to immediate post-surgical management

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: What postoperative pulmonary complication risk is particularly important in obese ICU patients or those with COPD?
answer: Preventing postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) including atelectasis, pneumonia, and respiratory failure is critical in obese and COPD patients
rationale: Reduced functional residual capacity, impaired mucociliary clearance, and diminished respiratory reserve make obese and COPD patients highly vulnerable to PPCs.
confusable_with: Cardiac complications being the dominant post-op risk in all patients

domain: Anesthesia critical care (shock & resuscitation, sepsis, ARDS & mechanical ventilation, hemodynamic monitoring, AKI, sedation/delirium, nutrition, end-of-life)
stem: In ICU patients with thyroid storm, why is aspirin avoided for temperature management?
answer: Aspirin is not recommended in thyroid storm because it may displace thyroid hormone from plasma carrier proteins, worsening thyrotoxicosis
rationale: Aspirin competes for thyroid hormone binding sites on thyroxine-binding globulin, increasing free T4/T3 levels and potentially exacerbating the storm.
confusable_with: Aspirin being safe for fever management in all ICU patients
